source_refs.note: Book p. 59-60: 2.12 Differentials, definition dy = f'(x)dx and Example 24

blocks.text: Bachon, ab tak aap \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko ek hi symbol samajhte aaye hain, jis ka matlab derivative hai. Aaj hum \(dx\) aur \(dy\) ko alag alag matlab denge, aur yeh dikhayenge ke in dono ka ratio phir bhi derivative hi rehta hai. Yeh idea agle sabaq mein andaze (approximation) aur ghalti (error) nikalne ke kaam aayega.

Kitab kehti hai: maan lein \(f\) point \(x\) par differentiable hai. Agar \(dx\) ek independent variable (azaad variable, jise hum khud chunte hain) ho, jo 0 ke qareeb (neighborhood mein) values le sakta hai lekin khud 0 nahi, to hum dependent variable \(dy\) ko is formula se define karte hain:

blocks.text_alt: d y equals f prime of x times d x, equation (1)

blocks.text: Kyun ke \(dx \ne 0\), hum (1) ki dono sides ko \(dx\) se divide kar sakte hain:

blocks.text_alt: d y over d x equals f prime of x

blocks.text: Is tarah humara maqsad poora ho gaya: \(dy\) aur \(dx\) aise define ho gaye ke un ka ratio derivative \(f'(x)\) ke barabar hai. Yahi wajah hai ke \(dx\) ko 0 nahi liya: zero se divide nahi kar sakte.

Aasaan alfaaz mein:
\(dx\) (\(x\) ka differential) koi bhi chhota sa non-zero number hai jo hum khud chunte hain, yani \(x\) mein qadam.
\(dy\) (\(y\) ka differential) phir hisaab se nikalta hai: \(dy = f'(x)\,dx\), yani slope ganna qadam.
Misaal se samjhein: agar ek seerhi (slope) har ek meter aage chalne par 0.3 meter upar jati ho, aur aap 2 meter aage chalein, to aap \(0.3 \times 2 = 0.6\) meter upar gaye. Yahan 0.3 slope \(f'(x)\) hai, 2 qadam \(dx\) hai, aur 0.6 woh \(dy\) hai.
Graph par \(dy\) yeh hai ke tangent line \(dx\) aage jane par kitna upar uthti hai. Agle sabaq (2.12.1) mein dekhenge ke yeh curve ke asal uthne ke bohat qareeb hota hai.
blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text:
Differential nikalne ka tareeqa: aam tareeqe se differentiate karein, phir derivative ke baad \(dx\) likh dein.
Misaal: \(y = x^{2}\) ho to \(dy = 2x\,dx\); \(y = \sin x\) ho to \(dy = \cos x\,dx\); \(y = e^{x}\) ho to \(dy = e^{x}\,dx\).
blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text:
\(y = x^{3}\) ka differential kya hai, aur \(x = 2\), \(dx = 0.01\) par us ki value kya hogi?
(Jawab: \(dy = 3x^{2}\,dx\), aur value \(3(4)(0.01) = 0.12\).)
blocks.title: Khud sochiye

blocks.text: Ab kitab ki Example 24 dekhte hain. Is mein do hisse hain: pehle formula ki shakal mein \(dy\), phir numbers rakh kar us ki value.

blocks.title: Example 24
blocks.problem:
(a) Find \(dy\) if \(y = x^{4} + 7x\).
(b) Find the value of \(dy\) when \(x = 1\) and \(dx = 0.1\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x^{4} + 7x\); part (b) mein \(x = 1\), \(dx = 0.1\).
Maloom karna: (a) \(dy\) ka formula; (b) us ki value.
Tareeqa: definition \(dy = f'(x)\,dx\). Pehle \(f'(x)\) nikalenge, phir use \(dx\) se multiply karenge. Bas itna hi kaam hai.

(a) Qadam 1: Derivative nikalein
\[f(x) = x^{4} + 7x\]
\[f'(x) = 4x^{3} + 7 \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: har term par power rule: \(x^{4}\) ka derivative \(4x^{3}\) (power aage aayi, ek kam ho gayi), aur \(7x\) ka derivative 7.

Qadam 2: Differential likhein
\[dy = f'(x)\,dx\]
\[dy = (4x^{3} + 7)\,dx \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: definition yahi kehti hai: derivative ko \(dx\) se multiply karo to \(dy\) milta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(dx\) likhna mat bhooliye; \(dy = 4x^{3} + 7\) likhna ghalat hai, woh to \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai.

(b) Qadam 3: (2) mein \(x = 1\), \(dx = 0.1\) rakhein
\[dy = (4(1)^{3} + 7)(0.1)\]
\[= 11(0.1) = 1.1\]
Kyun: \(dy\) do cheezon par depend karta hai: point \(x\) kahan hai aur qadam \(dx\) kitna bara hai. Dono rakh diye to number mil gaya.

Tasdeeq:
(2) ko \(dx\) se divide karein to \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 4x^{3} + 7\), yani derivative, jaisa definition chahti hai. \(x = 1\) par slope 11 hai, aur \(11 \times 0.1 = 1.1\). Jawab theek hai.

blocks.text: Example 24 se yeh samjhein: part (a) ka jawab ek formula hai jis mein \(x\) aur \(dx\) dono hain, aur part (b) mein dono ki value rakhne se ek number mila. Exam mein agar sirf "find \(dy\)" poocha jaye to formula likhna hai; agar values di hon to number nikalna hai.

1. \(dx\) ek azaad, chhota, non-zero number hai; \(dy = f'(x)\,dx\) dono, \(x\) aur \(dx\), par depend karta hai.
2. \(dx\) se divide karein to wapas \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f'(x)\) milta hai.
3. \(dy\) nikalne ke liye: differentiate karein, phir \(dx\) se multiply karein.
4. \(dy\) ki numerical value ke liye point \(x\) aur qadam \(dx\) dono chahiye.
blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein

blocks.text:
1. \(dx\) likhna bhool jana: \(dy = 4x^{3} + 7\) ghalat hai, yeh to \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai.
2. Value nikalte waqt \(x\) ki jagah \(dx\) ki value daal dena, ya ulta. Pehle likh lijiye ke \(x\) kya hai aur \(dx\) kya.
blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
